sites.functional_impact_measured: Receptor expressed and purified; cryo-EM structure of A3AR–Gi complex resolved, demonstrating intact G protein coupling. Expression was enhanced relative to unmodified construct.
sites.rationale: ADORA3 has no signal peptide (raw topology begins with 'O', landmarks assign residues 1–14 as EXTRACELLULAR), so residue 1 (M) is the mature N-terminus and the only extracellular terminus available for a prepend tag. No residue number is stated in the ledger clip, but exactly one extracellular terminus exists, making the position topology-derived rather than validated. The 14-residue extracellular N-terminal span (1–14) provides ≥3 residues of clearance from TM1 (begins at residue 15). The construct was functional: a cryo-EM complex with Gi was resolved, confirming G protein coupling was preserved. Full-length human A3AR (UniProt P0DMS8) expressed in Sf9 insect cells with a FLAG epitope prepended at the N-terminus; the first 22 aa of human M4 mAChR were inserted as a spacer between the FLAG and native A3AR residue 1 to enhance expression. The construct was used to obtain a cryo-EM structure of the A3AR–G protein complex.

literature_notes: L2 and L3 describe the same human A3AR FLAG-N-terminus / His-C-terminus construct as L1 (same paper, PMC12361428); L1 was chosen as the primary supporting clip. L4 (sheep A3R ortholog, PMC11544091) independently corroborates an N-terminal FLAG on a full-length membrane-anchored A3R, but is indirect (different species) and was not used as the primary clip. The C-terminal fusions (L5, L6) and the C-terminal His tag (L2) all land in the intracellular tail (residues 285–318) and are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an insertion in ECL1 (73–83), ECL2 (150–177), or ECL3 (253–261) of ADORA3 or a close ortholog, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: LgBiT (large NanoLuc domain) fused to the C-terminus of full-length A3AR; residues 285–318 are intracellular per topology landmarks, so this fusion is cytoplasmic, not a surface tag site.
